newsitem.title: USA: CME plans overhaul of milk futures contract.
newsitem.headline: CME plans overhaul of milk futures contract.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange on May 22 will convert its physically delivered fluid milk contracts to cash-settled basis formula price (BFP) futures and options, the CME said in a release.

Listing of the new contracts, for every calendar month, will begin with the July 1997 contract, pending approval by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. The CME introduced fluid milk futures January 11, 1996.

The new contract will use BFP, the U.S. Agriculture Department's monthly average price for manufacturing grade milk. Like those of fluid milk, BFP contracts are based on Grade A cow's milk traded in 200,000 lb units.
"By moving to a national average, we believe this contract will have much broader national appeal than the existing contract," said Robert Prosi, CME Dairy Products Committee chairman.
Interest in fluid milk futures waned after a modest start and currently there is no open interest in the contract.
The BFP is the focal point of pricing in the entire dairy industry, the release stated.
